_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); oil and gas producer signals

pit_profile.why: FY13 10-K: 'We are an independent oil and natural gas company currently focused on the acquisition, development, exploration and exploitation of unconventional, onshore oil and natural gas reserves in the Permian Basin in West Texas.' Risk factors: 'The oil and natural gas industry is cyclical, which can result in shortages of drilling rigs, equipment, raw materials (particularly sand and other proppants), supplies and personnel.' and 'Our revenues, operating results, profitability, future rate of growth and the carrying value of our oil and natural gas properties depend significantly upon the prevailing prices for oil and natural gas.' The kind is CYCLICAL on the 10-K's own word for its industry (the CB and LYB rule): the earnings are the oil price; of the live disruption themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution': none names an oil and gas producer

The kind is CYCLICAL on the 10-K's own word for its industry (the CB and LYB rule): the earnings are the oil price; of the live disruption themes, OFFSHORE is scoped to 'lower-cost offshore delivery (Indian IT services) takes share and price from Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing', CLOUD to 'public cloud displaces on-premise hardware, storage, legacy databases and data-center outsourcing', ECOMMERCE to 'e-commerce (Amazon effect) displaces physical retail, malls, grocery, distribution': none names an oil and gas producer. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.14x; +62% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.86; conservative 2yr +326%.

BEAR.desc: Flat EPS (no EPS change in FY13-FY13 to measure: the 0% cap); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +140.7%/yr (Q3 revenues + margin + buyback); P/E at its 2.1-yr ex-FY12 median

BULL.desc: EPS +140.7%/yr (no FY13-FY13 CAGR to measure: BASE's rate); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +140.7%/yr (no 2-yr run in FY13-FY13: BULL's rate); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: FANG (retrospective, 2015-02-06) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.14x (64.7% downside to Bear $25 / +464.7% upside to Bull $400) | Adj composite 2.96 vs market 1.10: gap +1.86 [UNDERVALUED] | +61% above the EPP floor $44 (34x FY14E $1.29) | Conservative 2-yr case: +325.5% total (+162.7%/yr) | At 54.9x FY14E the 15% hurdle price $94 sits at or below the BASE case; oil-equivalent production +177.9% and oil production +176.9% in Q3 2014, forward revenues +140.7% (no FY14 revenue guide in numbers, Q3 2014 revenues as reported); no theme in the registry is live for an oil and gas producer on this date; none has dated evidence.
